title: How Likely After the Fix: Fault Trees, the Average Chance a Safety Function Is Dead, and Why Common Cause Limits Redundancy

questions.question: A protection's chance of failing is not known (NaN). How should the arithmetic treat it?
options: As 1: not knowing is not a small chance, and the protection is counted as failed
As 0: an unknown chance cannot be counted against the design
As 0.5, the middle of the range
It is skipped, and the others are multiplied
questions.explanation: A protection whose reliability nobody knows cannot be relied on. Counting it as certain to fail means it earns nothing until someone finds the number.

questions.question: What is a single point of failure in a fault tree?
options: The basic event with the largest probability
The top event itself
A basic event that on its own causes the top event: one reached through or nodes only
Any event under an all_of node
questions.explanation: If nothing else has to go wrong at the same time, that one failure is the accident. The welded contactor was one until a second was put in series.

questions.question: Why is the average chance a function is dead about half of rate times interval, and when is that wrong?
options: It is exact at every interval
Over the interval it rises from zero to its end value
It is half the failure rate, whatever the interval
It understates the chance, by 31 percent at ten years
questions.explanation: The shortcut overstates it when rate times interval is not small: 31 percent too high at ten years. The chance of being dead grows from nothing just after a test to its largest just before the next, and a demand can come at any time. The straight line shortcut overshoots once the curve bends.

questions.question: With 10 percent common cause, how much better is a second channel than one?
options: 275 times: the two fail independently
No better: common cause takes all the gain
Twice: two channels, half the chance
10 times: the beta term is nearly all of the answer
questions.explanation: A tenth of the failures take both channels at once. That share times the single channel's pfd swamps the squared term, so the gain is 10 and not 275.

questions.question: G2 went from beta 0.10 to beta 0.02 and stayed in the same class. What does that say?
options: Beta makes no difference to the pfd
The calculation was wrong at one of the two betas
A fivefold cut in beta is too small to measure
The improvement was real, 4.4 times lower pfd, but did not cross a band
questions.explanation: Classes are coarse, and the numbers matter more than the class. The pfd fell from 3.75e-04 to 8.56e-05. Both land in the band for likelihood 2, so the class is the same, and the numbers are what show the gain.

questions.question: With the ideal pair, the product scores 4, which reads low. What is the class and why?
options: low: 4 is in the low band
medium: a severity of 4 is never classed lower, and a catastrophe's residual risk has to be accepted by a named person, not computed away
high: any catastrophe is high
unacceptable, until tested weekly
questions.explanation: The floor of 19-01 holds whatever the arithmetic gives. What is left of a risk of death is accepted in writing by a named person.
